retentionRecord.summary: The input fingerprint is byte-identical. All 240 candidate dispositions are retained, with one added. Retained byte-identical: 227 of 233 surfaces, 126 of 143 compact claims, and all 7 applied translation repairs. Names, roles, historicity and descriptors are retained for all 66 people except p059. Every other change to an existing person row is the active-date (a) or related-person (r) hint field. The 17 changed claims are the 16 legacy kinship relationship rows, restated as 13 v7 family edges on the same evidence, and the corrected p041 title.

ownerFindings.summary: The inherited identification of the BC 154 chancellor 青翟 as Zhuang Qingdi (莊青翟) contradicts Hanshu 19 and Hanshu 42. Zhuang (Yan) Qingdi was chancellor under Emperor Wu, and Tao Qing held the office in BC 154. The candidate keeps the source form, records a conflict claim, and proposes removing "Zhuang" from both English fields.

Seven misattributed surface occurrences were removed and one candidate disposition was added: the Lü clan (s0010); the throne declined twice (s0036); a proverb (s0049); a sought heirship (s0118); a verb (s0204); and a temple name (s0389).

Four rows were added. p067 is Yuan Ang's elder brother, the friend of the Marquis of Jiang. p068 is Zhong's father, an elder brother of Yuan Ang; he is not merged with p067 because the chapter does not show that they are the same brother. p069 is Master □, a named diviner whose surname graph is lost. p070 is Ju Meng's mother.
Han Gaozu had two unlinked chunk records (p015 高帝 and p039 高皇帝); a same-person pair was added. The eight existing duplicate-chunk same-person pairs are retained.
汝陰侯 is the Marquis of Ruyin, not Ruoyin (claim value only; the current English is already correct).

The text and Hanshu 19 give only 歐/敺 as the Minister of Justice. The inherited reading "Zhang Ou" is plausible and is not contradicted, but this chapter does not establish it. It is retained and flagged in coverage.unresolvedReferences for the identity reviewer.

chronology.conventions: BC conversions use local annal witnesses where available: Wen 3 = BC 177, Wen 6 = BC 174, Wen 15 = BC 165, Wen Later 7 = BC 157, Jing 2 = BC 155, Jing 3 = BC 154 (Hanshu 4 and 5). 孝文時 is BC 180-157 (Emperor Wen enthroned BC 180, after Empress Lü died). 高後時 is BC 188-180, 景帝時 is BC 157-141, and 建元 is BC 140-135. Yuan Ang's post-rising retirement and death are bounded BC 154-141 because s0106 places them after the Wu-Chu defeat. Retrospective exemplars receive undated attestations plus a retrospective-reference event; the date of the later speech is never copied onto the recalled person. No Western date is invented for an undated person, and no research hold is used where the source simply gives no temporal wording.

ownerProposals.before: Yuan Ang said: "Rank exists for a reason; you have named a queen, and Lady Shen is a concubine—lord and servant cannot share one bench.
ownerProposals.after: Yuan Ang said: "Rank exists for a reason; you have named an empress, and Lady Shen is a concubine—a concubine and her mistress cannot share one bench.
ownerProposals.reason: 后 is the empress, and 妾、主 contrasts the concubine with her mistress, not a lord with a servant.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: When Yuan Ang was hemmed in at Wu, that same clerk was deputy marshal of his guard; he spent his savings on two hundred liters of spirits, and on a bitter day when the men were parched and starving he feasted the southwest watch until they collapsed drunk.
ownerProposals.after: When Yuan Ang was hemmed in at Wu, that same clerk was deputy marshal of his guard; he spent his savings on two piculs of strong ale, and on a bitter day when the men were parched and starving he feasted the southwest watch until they collapsed drunk.
ownerProposals.reason: 二石醇醪 is two piculs (shi) of strong ale; "two hundred liters of spirits" invents a metric conversion and distilled liquor.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: Ang was unhappy at heart; many strange things happened in his house, and he therefore went to a certain diviner's place to inquire by divination.
ownerProposals.after: Ang was unhappy at heart; many strange things happened in his house, and he therefore went to the place of Master □ (the surname graph is lost) to inquire by divination.
ownerProposals.reason: □生 is a named Master whose surname graph is lost in the text; "a certain diviner" drops the name.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: Uneasy in mind and troubled by omens at home, he went to a fortune-teller for a reading.
ownerProposals.after: Uneasy in mind and troubled by omens at home, he went to Master □ (the surname is lost in the text) for a reading.
ownerProposals.reason: □生 is a named Master whose surname graph is lost in the text; "a fortune-teller" drops the name.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: The Art of War says, "Victory rests in the general, not in wishful thinking."
ownerProposals.after: The military treatises say, "Victory rests in the general, not in wishful thinking."
ownerProposals.reason: 兵法 is the military canon generally; the quotation is not identified as The Art of War.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: Raise inner and outer ramparts a hundred fifty paces apart, stock rolling logs, sow caltrops, and dig a killing ditch between the rings.
ownerProposals.after: Raise high walls and deep moats, stock stones for throwing, sow caltrops, and build a second wall inside, a hundred fifty paces from the outer one.
ownerProposals.reason: 藺石 are stones for throwing, 高城深塹 is high walls and deep moats, and 復為一城其內 adds an inner wall; "rolling logs" and "a killing ditch" are invented.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.before: Issue seed, ploughs, and roof-timber first, then fill the sites with convicts and men buying out penal labor;
ownerProposals.after: Build houses and supply farm tools first, then fill the sites with convicts and with pardoned men still serving labor terms;
ownerProposals.reason: 先為室屋，具田器 is houses and farm tools (no seed); 免徒復作 are released convicts serving remitted labor, not men buying out their labor.
ownerProposals.author: owner

ownerProposals.author: owner
